findings.summary: Reviewed commit 461615a for CODEX-04-A against the approved card, architecture v1.2 (SHA-256 02adc2e0…, ADR-E02/E05, WM-04: saving is separate from production, idempotency comes before quota/CAS, the source is stored before interpretation, and durability uses an independent journal) and the bounded handoff. All three acceptance criteria are met and supported by real evidence on the reviewed tree. The child's original question and the parent's context are stored as separate, unaltered UTF-16 fields, kept apart from any interpretation, with append-only corrections. Repeated SAVE actions reuse the same command key, are guarded by an in-flight flag and disabled buttons, and do not duplicate across lost responses, retries and reloads; Submit is correctly left to 04-B. The UI shows clear offline/unsent/pending wording, and a saved-only wonder states it has no 24-hour deadline. Evidence: 77/77 tests, the build, the protected check_application_card probe, and a source-pinned CUA run covering all 8 native scenarios (320px phone, keyboard focus, offline retry, reload and reconcile, sibling isolation, withdrawal). Open gates are kept and stated: WM-01/WM-13 scheduler and operator alert, 04-B receipt/once-only booking (rows 305/306), 04-C, 09-C, and production durability, identity and privacy.

findings.title: Pre-commit 503 (journal_unavailable) shown as possibly-lost response
findings.problem: Every status other than 403, 409 and 429 goes to 'Not confirmed saved. The response may have been lost… retry the original command.' A journal_unavailable 503 can mean the server refused the command before committing anything, for example after a journal failure in another tab or session. The copy is still truthful ('not confirmed saved'), but it suggests a lost commit and encourages retries that will keep failing until the pending command is reconciled. The usual path is blocked by writes_closed, so the effect is small.
findings.fix_check: A 503 that the server marks as not committed gets its own message that points to the pending/reconcile path, or the reason for keeping the current behaviour is documented.

findings.title: Household-wide write closure but pending list filtered to acting adult
findings.problem: writes_closed is true whenever any household command is unacknowledged. However, pending and saved only include commands from the current adult, child and consent epoch. A second adult in the same household would see 'New saves paused' with nothing to reconcile until the first adult reconciles. This is local fixture behaviour with one adult per household and is consistent with 'owned' in the handoff, but it should be recorded for WM-01/WM-13 scheduler reconciliation.
findings.fix_check: REPORT or the contract notes cross-adult pending visibility as part of the WM-01/WM-13 integration gate, or the UI tells the user that another family member's pending command is blocking saves.

findings.title: Whole-file reformatting of accepted adult-http.mjs
findings.problem: The behavioural changes are small and stricter: optional capture routes, a per-route 65536-byte limit, and checks that content-length is a safe integer and matches the body size. But the file was rewritten into a compressed one-line style, which makes it harder to confirm that the accepted guards are unchanged. Existing adult HTTP regressions still pass, including the old 4096-byte limit (413 at 5000 bytes is tested).
findings.fix_check: Future edits to accepted files keep the existing formatting, or include a diff with whitespace changes ignored as evidence.
